stage_status.note: CORRECTED AUDIT 2026-10-02 (my earlier pass blamed FX2 framing and called this BLK2-sized - both wrong; these are the measured facts). The 3 failures are artifacts/scale_board_0{2,3,4}/verdict.json: identical image sha 90bae737a378, cases[] empty, error "framing/length 0 vs 8218" - the board returned ZERO bytes. board/run_scale_board.py reads replies over the DOCK UART at 115200, and this rig has no UART return path at all (measured and recorded in board/eth_rate_harness/eth_rate_harness.v header: ttyUSB1 RX empty at 4 baud rates, ttyUSB0 echoes only its own TX). So this is the dead-serial-console condition that motivated the RMII harness, not scaler arithmetic and not a bandwidth ceiling (8218 B is 0.72 s at 115200, well inside the 20 s read timeout). Porting it to RMII is the right closure but is NOT a BLK2 fit: the reply is 8218 B against BLK2's fixed 532 B / 128-word capture (17 chunks), the config is 4 fields (cfg_in_w/in_h/out_w/out_h, up to 12b each = 48b > the 32-bit config_word), and cfg_valid is only accepted between frames with cfg_done ~56 cycles later. Needs chunked frame readout + a 2-word config, i.e. a new request shape. [prior text: scale_poly6 remote attempts FAILED: framing/length 0 vs 8218 (scale_board_02..04) - harness protocol mismatch under investigation 138K Pro SoM P&R evidence added; see target_boards and route_timing_gw5a138.]

stage_status.note: ccm_stream is harness CORE 8, and the 2026-10-02 port-level audit underestimated its adapter need by 202 writes: "only the 3x3 matrix needs cfg_addr/cfg_wdata table writes (9 words)" is true of the matrix alone, but ccm_stream validates the WHOLE shadow image at commit, so a 9-word load either leaves the node banks at their identity default (making every tone-curve case vacuous) or is rejected.  The harness therefore writes ctrl + 9 matrix + 3 bias + 99 lin + 99 enc = 211 beats and then pulses cfg_commit.  CONFIG also cannot wait for cfg_done the way the other seven cores do: a legal commit applies only at a presented SOF with an empty pipe, which here is the block's FIRST RUN beat -- strictly after CONFIG ends.  So the loader leaves on a bounded legality window (the core scans 99 flat node indices one per cycle) and requires cfg_pending still high at that point, because pending_apply is what a legal commit sets; a core that neither errored nor armed a pending apply is held until the 4095-cycle CONFIG window and comes back as config-rejected instead of hanging.  The core has NO saturation output port -- quantize() clamps to [0,MPX] silently -- so flags[7] is structurally 0 here and clip coverage is impossible by construction.  What replaces it: every case is asserted clamp-free against the model's PRE-clamp quantization (protocol.expected_clip), so a saturating case fails loudly rather than agreeing with a low flag, and the generated sweep band [96,160] per channel is the range all eight bundles are provably clamp-free over.  Simulation evidence/ccm_20261002_140446_225060: 42 requests = 32 numerically verified blocks (bundles 0-7 x 8/16/32/64 pixels, stalls rotated 0/1/7, every one flags 0, words in == words out) + 6 malformed + 2 config-reject (cfg 8, i.e. the bundle index the table does not have, and a high-bit poison) + 1 count-mismatch + 1 STAT poll.  Throughput: 64 pixels in 70 cycles at stall 0 (~1.09 cycles/pixel = II 1 plus the 5-stage latency), consistent with the SPEC.  Gate evidence/ccm_gate1: 62.50/70.44 MHz against the 50 MHz floor, lut 14691 (routed LUT4 14755) of the 15000 budget, dsp 0 -- so ISP-14's "no multiplier primitive" claim holds inside a full harness image, not just standalone; bitstream 51e1157aefa4, and its eth_rate_harness.v is byte-identical to the RTL the session run below simulated.  CROSS-BLOCK SESSIONS are proven in simulation too, and the argument is a differential, not a pass count: evidence/ccm_20261002_145109_629663 is 54 requests = 32 blocks + 12 session cases (three phases of four: rsvd=0 controls, a rsvd=1 phase whose blocks ASK for bundle 5 while still running bundle 0, and a rsvd=3 phase that re-commits mid-session) + the same rejects.  What persists here is the APPLIED BUNDLE, which changes what a session block must differ from: on a streaming, stateless core a rsvd=3 block gives the same numbers as a fresh reset under that bundle, so the old "must differ from the unpersisted answer" guard would have rejected a perfectly good RECONFIG case; each case now names the interpretation it falsifies (rsvd=1 vs an image that configures every block, rsvd=3 vs an image that skips CONFIG), build_plan raises if the two answers coincide, and framediff's sim still passes on the same shared check_reply.  NOT covered, and not claimed: session cases on HARDWARE (run_eth_round only models CORE 7's reference RAM, and it now refuses --sessions for any other core rather than silently emitting an empty session group -- note the trap it refuses: a PERSIST block on CORE 8 runs the PREVIOUS bundle while the oracle would use that block's own config_word), the cfg_addr>=0x0D / >0x72 / >0xE2 address-error paths (the loader only ever writes legal addresses), and BITS=10.  board_test stays BLOCKED by dock power only; program evidence/ccm_gate1 for the first round.

stage_status.note: the old blocker ("framediff needs 2 frames - needs two-image adapter") was about the block shape, not the arithmetic.  The harness resets the core between blocks and this core's reference RAM *is* the state under test, so one block now carries FOUR 4x4 frames -- 64 words, the same budget CORE 5 already spends on one 8x8 image -- and the cross-frame behaviour lives inside it.  framediff_stream is harness CORE 7.  Proven over RMII/UDP in simulation (evidence/fd_sim1, re-run in fd_gate1): 32 numerically verified blocks covering all 16 fd_cfg bundles, 7 malformed/config rejects, count-mismatch and STAT poll all clean, 64 words in = 64 out, cycles 66 at stall 0 (64 pixels + the core's 2-cycle latency, tail-stripped report).  25 of those result words carry the scene_change bit, so seeding, a mid-block scene change and BOTH recovery policies (RESET and FAST_ADAPT) were checked against isp/framediff/models/model.py, never against the RTL.  Gate: evidence/fd_gate1 91.58/78.65 MHz against the 50 MHz floor, lut 4960, dsp 0, bitstream fefc15ea2e40.  CROSS-BLOCK PERSIST has since been built into the harness (rsvd byte: bit0 leaves the core unreset and steps over CONFIG, bit1 re-commits a new bundle on that unreset core; rsvd=2 and rsvd>3 are malformed), so the same four frames also travel as four one-frame blocks.  evidence/fd_persist1 proves that in simulation: 8 session blocks plus 4 unpersisted controls of the identical frames, every one flags 0 with 16 words in and 16 out at cycles 18.  The differential is the evidence, not the pass count: the controls answer the seed value 0, the persisted blocks answer the real frame-to-frame difference, and the mid-session re-config group answers the running background (50, 49, 58) -- three mutually exclusive answer sets, so an image that ignored rsvd could satisfy at most one.  build_plan refuses to emit a persisted case whose model answer equals the unpersisted one, which keeps the check from silently going vacuous, and a session block gets one attempt only (a re-send would advance the reference frame again).  NOT covered, and not claimed: a mid-session GEOMETRY change (the harness drives one fixed 4x4 raster with a table-free config word, so W/H cannot vary), any frame larger than 4x4, BITS=10, and the core's o_error path beyond "never fires" (reported sticky in result bit 10, model predicts 0, so a marker violation surfaces as a numeric mismatch).  Gate of the session-capable image: evidence/fd_persist1 106.54/85.68 MHz, lut 4975, dsp 0, bitstream 4459e1ab548d.  board_test is blocked by dock power only (192.168.137.16 unreachable at 2026-10-02T03:56Z: ping exit=1, no ARP entry while the host self-ping answers); program evidence/fd_persist1 for the first round -- fd_gate1 predates PERSIST and answers a session request as malformed, which the host uses as the image-version probe.
